objective: Close M134's highest-priority macro-interface gap with an executable fixed-one-cycle request/response contract, echoed transaction token, stored base-bank rotation, and two-entry elastic return FIFO.

architecture.maximum_admitted_issue_rate: one accepted read per clock when response consumer sustains service

expected_pass_line: PASS M136 one-cycle tagged 16-bank response bridge VCS requests=128 outputs=128 words=2048 ii1=120 stalls=12 fifo_full=12 row_crossings=120 wrong_token=1 missing=1 unsolicited=1 illegal_base=1 reset_recoveries=4 fifo_depth=2 latency=1 macro=false physical_speedup=false system_speedup=false headline=false
paper_safe_statement: Commercial VCS validates a fixed-one-cycle, transaction-token-checked 16-bank return bridge over 128 requests, 2,048 logical words, sustained interval-one request traces, two-entry backpressure, and four fail-closed attacks. The token must be supplied by a macro wrapper; per-bank data skew, actual SRAM macros, variable latency, wiring, energy and system speedup remain unadmitted.
prohibited_claims: Do not imply that foundry SRAM macros natively echo the M136 transaction token.
Do not generalize a fixed-one-cycle wrapper to arbitrary SRAM latency or clock-domain crossing.
Do not convert interval-one request service into physical or system speedup without matched macro timing and cycle simulation.
